messages: marta: Heads-up — new quant4b_rev1 reranker (surface bring-up) shows a clear MRR regression on short queries while NDCG@10 looks roughly the same. Suspect candidate normalization/tokenization mismatch introduced in the ingest pipeline :thinking: kevin: numbers? short queries meaning length < 8 tokens? marta: quick snapshot from yesterday's smoke run (fp16 -> quant4b_rev1): ``` # eval cohort: short_queries_v2 (len<=7) model fp16 -> MRR: 0.421, NDCG@10: 0.732 model quant4b -> MRR: 0.388, NDCG@10: 0.729 %drop ~7.8% in MRR, ndcg ~0.4% absolute ``` shubha: hmm. 7.8% MRR drop is large. Did we change candidate preproc or html stripping recently? I remember a small patch to keep metadata tags for structured fields. sam: I ran a quick diff on candidates_v1 vs candidates_v2: we now keep blocks unescaped in v2, which changes token counts for some short answers. sample diff: "answer":"42" -> "answer":"42" after earlier strip — could affect kv-cache alignment in short ctx. :eyes: nate: also check tokenizer version — tokenizers bump to 0.12.4 last week changed subword splits for < and > sequences. If quant runtime expects exact input tokenization parity with fp16 we get embed misalignment. marta: good point. command I used to repro: `python -m eval.run --cohort short_queries_v2 --model quant4b_rev1 --candidates candidates_v2.json --seed 42 --metric mrr,ndcg` eval-bot: automated-run: https://ci.redwood/evals/1776000123/quant4b_rev1-short-queries (logs + per-query csv). kevin: can you also run baseline fp16 against candidates_v2 (not v1)? need to know if candidate change alone explains drop or if quant interacts badly. marta: running fp16@candidates_v2 now, ETA ~20m. posting interim small sample: ``` sample id 12345: fp16_rank=1 (score 0.82), quant_rank=3 (scores: 0.47,0.45,0.44) text snippet: "How to reset API key?" -> candidate text had leading "\n" in v2 for some docs. ``` shubha: leading newlines matter for our sentencepiece model since it alters first-token classification; small but can flip top1. Could be why MRR suffers more than ndcg. sam: action idea: run two quick A/Bs: (A) quant4b_rev1 + normalization=v1 (strip html + trim whitespace) (B) quant4b_rev1 + normalization=v2. If A matches fp16 baseline then we know normalization is culprit. marta: agreed. kicking off both now with 5000-sample mini-cohort. kevin: also add a run with fp16 + normalization=v2 to check interaction (quad matrix). nate: logging note — include tokenizer version in metadata, and capture token counts per candidate (first 10) so we can quickly compare distributions. marta: added metadata flags: `tokenizer=spm-1.3.0`, `tokenizer_sha=abc123`, `normalizer=v2-keep-code`. (10 minutes pass) marta: interim results: mini-cohort (5k) - fp16 + norm=v1 -> MRR 0.423 - fp16 + norm=v2 -> MRR 0.422 - quant4b + norm=v1 -> MRR 0.419 - quant4b + norm=v2 -> MRR 0.387 => quant+v2 combo is the outlier. Looks like quantized weights amplify a mismatch caused by v2 normalization. shubha: that pattern suggests quant sensitivity to tokenization boundary shifts (maybe embedding table index rounding). We should try a short run with forced tokenized inputs (pre-tokenize and pass ids) to see if runtime tokenization is the issue. sam: good call — if pre-tokenized inputs remove delta then runtime tokenization or tokenizer version is the root cause. If not, quant kernels might be non-linear for these short contexts. marta: starting pretokenized run now (same cohort). eval-bot: queued pretokenized job 1776000188 — expected finish ~10m. kevin: if pretokenized fixes it, short-term mitigation = force normalization=v1 for onboard until we patch pipeline. Long-term = make quant runtime accept tokenizer metadata and error on mismatch. nate: also file a small test in CI that compares token counts for canonical normalization across quant and fp16 builds. marta: notes/action items: - (marta) finish pretokenized run + post results in thread (ETA 12m) - (kevin) prepare rollback config to force norm=v1 for tiled onboarding (if needed) - (shubha) open issue on tokenizer bump + candidate normalization interaction with reproducer attached - (nate) add token-count check to eval CI (small PR) - (sam) if quant runtime requires metadata, file runtime feature request with examples kevin: thanks. tagging infra for a quick rollout hold if we need to flip normalization in prod: @infra-team :bell: marta: pretokenized run finished: results -> quant4b + pretokenized(norm=v2) -> MRR 0.421 (so matching fp16). shubha: bingo. That narrows it to tokenization/runtime mismatch. sam: conclusion: normalization v2 changed surface text which combined with tokenizer bump resulted in different tokenization at runtime; quant path relied on implicit tokenizer pipeline that diverged. Short-term: force pretokenize or revert norm=v2 for critical cohorts. Long-term: enforce tokenizer/version parity across builds and surface tokenizer sha in deployments. marta: filing PR to revert norm=v2 for onboarding smoke. putting a hold on promoting quant4b_rev1 until we ship the fix. kevin: cool — move to 'blocker' status for the onboard ticket until rollback or tokenization fix lands. marta: will update ticket and ping when done. :white_check_mark:
